name: 2017 livery (star)
description: White fuselage; behind the wing a deep blue sweep, edged in front by a pale gray band, rises from the belly to the crown at the fin and covers the tail; the fin blue with a large white star outline (the Transat star) that spills down onto the rear fuselage; 'Air transat' in blue over the forward windows; blue winglets with a small star.

notes: Added for Air Transat (Canadian leisure carrier) from A321LRs in 2025. The star is an outline (a ring of white round blue), drawn as a logo, not an area. Year of introduction not confirmed here; older A330s may carry the previous scheme. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on C-GOKF (A321LR, left, 2025-10-13), reading x between its doors: Air runs x 0.137-0.187 and transat 0.191-0.302, their baseline at the windows' top (y ~0.25) and capitals to y ~0.59 (they had been drawn from 0.43 to 0.89, above the window line). The two words are different lettering read as one line, so each side has its own pair: on the right (C-GOKC, 2025-02-27) it reads Air transat from the tail, Air at the aft end (the right had shown transat Air). Colours re-measured 2026-11-22 (the maintainer's sighting C-GOJC showed a lighter, brighter fin than drawn): on C-GOIK (2023) and C-GOKH (2026), each balanced against the fuselage's white in the same photo, the fin and tail read a bright azure (#1C7BA4 and #117EC9; drawn #1A80BE), not the royal blue drawn before (#0158BA, from C-GOKF, whose photo is heavily processed). The paint is a gradient, lighter toward the fin's top and darker low on the sweep's front edge; one blue is drawn. 'Air' is light blue and 'transat' navy (both had been drawn one mid blue).
